#870. F1 drivers back return of 'very cool' V8 engines in the future

Several Formula 1 drivers have backed the possibility of V8 engines returning to the sport as early as 2030; watch the Las Vegas GP weekend on Sky Sports F1, with Friday's practice sessions at 12.30am and 4pm

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Formula 1's drivers appear to be unanimous with the prospect of V8 engine returning to the sport in the 2030s.

Earlier this week, ahead of this weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix, FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem teased the possibility of V8 engines with the sound of a screaming F1 car with a caption: "You spoke, we listened. V8s coming soon."

The FIA also published graphics on social media which suggested an agreement in principle had been reached by themselves, Formula 1 management and the engine manufacturers for V8 engines to return from 2030, but the post was deleted.

The current regulations are set to run until 2031, which could be an explanation for the deleted post, while further details of the overall power unit, including whether an electrical element and a turbo will remain, need to be finalised.

"I'd love to see it. When I look at the old videos of the old engines, they give me goosebumps," said Mercedes driver George Russell.

"I think it's about just that high-pitched squeal that I'm missing from this era. The purists will say take away all electrical power, but I think when you look at how a lot of these cars have evolved in recent years, and the power output from some of these electrical motors these days, Formula 1 is going to continue to be the fastest race cars on the planet, you need to have it, that's just the reality.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

"You need to have some sort of hybrid, because the power you get, you can't really produce that just solely on internal combustion.

"If we go back to V8s, having some sort of electrical power as well, to give you that extra 400, 500 kilowatts to bring the cars to 1000+ horsepower, that's what we want.

"I think it's worth remembering as well actually, the final V8 era, they sounded awesome, but the cars, they actually weren't very fast. I don't think many people realise that."

New world champion Kimi Antonelli agreed with his Mercedes team-mate and claims "many people would look forward" to the return of V8 engines.

"It's going be very cool to go back to more old style. Also, the cars will get lighter even further, probably 70kg, which is immense," he said.

"Definitely, I think it's a very exciting regulation change. Of course, we have got to first do well in this one."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Max Verstappen has been critical of the current power units which are around 53 per cent battery powered and led to an unusual style of driving and racing at some tracks, with the drivers sometimes unable to push flat out in a traditional manner.

Verstappen, who warned driving in Las Vegas will be "painful" due to the long straights, feels the FIA have listened to the drivers and realised the 2026 regulations are "not what you want".

The four-time world champion stated he would get rid of the turbo in future power unit regulations, and effectively have a fully normally aspirated engine.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

"In some tracks then you're not allowed to race because it will be too loud because if it's up to me I would take the turbo off," he explained.

"I would get rid, maybe you can use it as a push to pass, but not too much of the battery side. But then on some tracks, you're not allowed to race, so fuel consumption goes up a lot without a turbo, so you need a bigger tank if you don't want to do refuelling in the races, so I understand that you want to have a turbo.

"If it's fully up to me, of course you go back to like a V10 or whatever. That sounds even better, but I know that not something realistic.

"This [news] is good. This is for sure in the right direction, but again, it's not confirmed yet. So there's still a few things I guess that they need to agree on."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Lewis Hamilton, Fernando Alonso, Nico Hulkenberg Sergio Perez and Valtteri Bottas are the only drivers who drove in the previous V8 era which ended in 2013.

Alonso said it's "frustrating" F1 has not had V8 engines since 2014, while Hamilton is keen to know more details about the proposed return of V8s.

"I think it's ultimately dependent on… it's all well going to V8. It depends on how they design it, regulation-wise, and going back to the good sound because that's I think been lacking since we've been in the V6 era," he said.

"Yeah, bring back the smaller exhaust and get that sound back.

"But you could have that, and as long as we don't have the engine dying halfway down the straight, then I think that'd be better."

#869. Arsenal Double winner Storey dies aged 81

Former Arsenal and England midfielder Peter Storey has died at the age of 81.

Storey made 501 appearances in all competitions for the Gunners between 1965 and 1977, scoring 17 goals.

He was part of the Double-winning Arsenal team which secured the First Division title and FA Cup in 1970-71 under manager Bertie Mee.

"Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of double winner Peter Storey," Arsenal said in a statement.

"All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time.

"We will pay our respects to Peter at our forthcoming home match against Borussia Dortmund."

Surrey-born Storey joined Arsenal as an apprentice in 1961 and made his first-team debut against Leicester City in 1965, initially starting his career at right-back before being moved into midfield.

He is currently eighth on Arsenal's list of all-time appearance holders and was capped 19 times by England, although he did not feature in a major tournament for the Three Lions.

Storey collected runners-up medals with Arsenal in the League Cup in 1967-68 and 1968-69 and in the FA Cup in 1971-72.

He joined Second Division Fulham on a free transfer in March 1977 and made 19 appearances for the Cottagers before his contract was terminated later that year and he retired.

However, Storey had something of a troubled life after his retirement from professional football.

He was convicted of running a brothel - for which he received a suspended prison sentence in 1979 - and was later jailed for three years for his involvement in a counterfeiting operation, then served another prison sentence in 1990 for attempting to smuggle pornographic videos into Britain.

#868. Azeez to Andrés: seven smart-looking Premier League deadline day deals

An 18-year-old who has played at two major international tournaments and the division’s top clearance maker from last season also feature

A tricky, exciting, quick and versatile midfielder, Azeez has proven himself in the Championship with Millwall over the past two seasons and now deserves a chance to test himself in the top flight.

Brighton had been chasing him for a while and struck a deal on deadline day for a very reasonable reported initial £12.5m, rising to £15m. If he can make the step up and produce anything like his second-tier form, he’ll be a steal.

He is a high-volume producer at the sharp end of the pitch, constantly making things happen that threaten the opposition’s goal, but standing out most for his crossing. He ranked top of the Championship last season for open-play crosses (227) and expected assists from crosses (6.71 xA).

He also ranked fourth for dribble attempts (131), ninth for shots (95), sixth for chances created from open play (58). He created good-quality chances, too; only two players created more big chances than he did (18), and he ranked fourth for expected assists. His 9.12 xA alongside only seven assists suggests he may benefit from playing alongside better finishers.

A hugely exciting prospect. Despite being 18, Mbaye has significant and noteworthy experience under his belt. Last year he made six appearances, including in the final, for Senegal at the Africa Cup of Nations and this summer he made four appearances at the World Cup. He has also played in two Ligue 1 title-winning campaigns, including 2024-25, when he became the youngest player in PSG’s history to start a game, and won the Champions League in both of those seasons

He is a dribbling and ball-carrying menace, who always looks as if he’s about to do something special. Among players to play at least 900 minutes in Ligue 1 last season, he was 11th for carries (moving at least five metres with the ball) per 90, with 20.0, and 12th for progressive carries (moving at least five metres upfield with the ball) per 90, with 10.3. Most of the players above him in both lists are defenders, who naturally have more space to move into.

He was third for take-on-ending carries, or running with the ball for at least five metres before attempting to beat an opponent with a dribble, with 2.9 per 90. And he also has end product to boot. He scored at Afcon and the World Cup despite limited minutes and his 0.45 goals or assists per 90 for PSG last season is not to be sniffed at.

Danso had a pretty impossible task over his two years at Tottenham. He was the back-up to the first-choice centre-backs Cristian Romero and Micky van de Ven, playing intermittently on both sides of central defence in dysfunctional teams jumping between styles of play, and he very rarely played for any consistent run of games.

He was unfairly compared with the players he was replacing for much of his time there, but the truth is he was always reliable enough. He excelled, however, when Romero got injured during the run-in last season and he was called upon in Spurs’ time of need as they scraped clear of relegation.

He may not be the best on the ball – though he is hardly terrible – but he is an excellent deep defender. Among those to play at least 1,000 minutes in the Premier League last season, Danso ranked first for clearances (8.2 per 90) and headed clearances (6.3), and was fifth for aerial duels won (4.8 per 90).

He could thrive at Sunderland, who spent more of their out-of-possession game time in a low block than any other team in the Premier League last season (25%). Danso could be perfectly at home in this setup, paired alongside the player he beat into second place for clearances and headed clearances: Dan Ballard.

It was always said during Pep Guardiola’s time at Manchester City that attackers had their wings clipped in terms of individual freedom, limited to playing within the parameters of the manager’s meticulous gameplan.

But dribbling ability became increasingly important in the final years of his reign, with Jérémy Doku and Antoine Semenyo on the wings and Rayan Cherki in between. Doku (162) and Semenyo (144) ranked first and second for dribbles attempted in the Premier League last season, with Cherki ninth (111). They also ranked first (84), fourth (59) and eighth (51), respectively, for dribbles completed.

With the deadline-day addition of Ndiaye, City have gone in even harder on dribbling ability under Enzo Maresca. The Senegal international ranked second for dribbles attempted (136) and dribbles completed (73) in the Premier League last season.

Fernandez-Pardo’s versatility is a major attraction. He’s comfortable playing off the left and cutting in on to his right foot, or as a No 9. Although not the bulkiest, he has explosive pace and promises to be a threat in behind.

The Belgium international is arguably at his most threatening when running with the ball because he does so with such purpose. His 122 carries progressing the ball at least 10 metres upfield in Ligue 1 last term were bettered by only seven players, several of whom were defenders.

On top of that, he ranked top for carries into the penalty area (69) and seventh for carries ending with a shot or chance created (39).

Fofana appeared to be enjoying a swift rise in 2024-25, only for a serious ankle injury to massively disrupt his development in 2025-26. Sunderland will be hoping they can get him back to the levels shown the season before last, when he was a real livewire on Lyon’s left flank.

He contributed nine goal involvements (five goals, four assists) in 1,586 minutes in Ligue 1 in 2024-25, averaging one every 176 minutes. Only eight forwards (900+ mins) averaged more expected assists per 90 (0.25).

The most eye-catching aspects of his game, however, were his dynamism and pace. He could be difficult to stop once moving, and this made him a very useful outlet. Among Ligue 1 forwards (900+ mins), his 16.6 carries per 90 ranked him sixth, and he moved up to third for progressive carries per 90 (11.5).

Fofana is direct, exciting and has significant potential. He is a player Sunderland could make a profit on if he reaches the levels previously expected.

Andrés arrived to bolster Brighton’s midfield options after Carlos Baleba’s exit to Manchester United. Although a different type of midfielder to the Cameroonian, Chema is another with vast potential.

A product of Real Madrid’s academy, Chema joined Stuttgart last summer. During his sole campaign in the Bundesliga, he was in and out of the team but caught the eye at the base of their midfield.

Comparisons have been made to Rodri because of his physical attributes and nominal role as a holding midfielder. He doesn’t have anything like the same influence in possession but Chema is tidy on the ball.

It’s what he offers defensively that is most notable, however. He’s been broadly praised for his anticipation and reading of the game, ranking second among midfielders (900+ mins) since the start of last season for interceptions per 90 in the Bundesliga (2.3).

#867. Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared

The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer

Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons

Key ins: Bruno Guimarães (Newcastle, £75m), Ezri Konsa (Aston Villa, £51m), Piero Hincapié (Bayer Leverkusen, £45m), Christos Tzolis (Club Brugge, £34m)

Key outs: Leandro Trossard (Besiktas, £15.3m), Jakub Kiwior (Porto, £14.5m), Gabriel Jesus (Barcelona, £8.6m), Fábio Vieira (Hamburg, £7.7m), Christian Nørgaard (Everton, £7m), Ethan Nwaneri (Borussia Dortmund, loan)

It is all change at Villa and, although a little trepidation is inevitable, a refresh was probably overdue. At the same time, Unai Emery did not want to lose so many key players and Villa’s manager has made clear there is no such thing as a transition season in his eyes. Villa have generated about £300m from the sales of nine players and brought in 10 at a cost of about £250m. Villa have lowered their wage bill and changed the profile of their squad. Zion Suzuki, Ibrahim Mbaye and Johan Manzambi, names on the lips of Villa’s rivals, are particularly exciting signings. Last summer there was concern Villa had gone stale and 12 months ago they ended up fretting on deadline day – Harvey Elliott and Jadon Sancho joined on loan – but there was no such chaos this time. Ben Fisher

Key ins: Johan Manzambi (Freiburg, £51m), Nicolas Jackson (Chelsea, £47.5m), Ibrahim Mbaye (PSG, £47m), João Gomes (Wolves, £34m), Zion Suzuki (Parma, £30m), Taylor Harwood-Bellis (Southampton, £25m), Matteo Ruggeri (Atlético Madrid, £21.4m), Leon Goretzka (Bayern Munich, free), Aaron Wan-Bissaka (West Ham, loan), Alejandro Garnacho (Chelsea, loan)

The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues?

Perhaps Bournemouth’s best business was keeping hold of their coveted key players, chiefly Eli Junior Kroupi, Rayan, Alex Scott and Tyler Adams. Bournemouth rejected bids from Chelsea for Scott and stayed true to their plan of resisting offers to give Marco Rose the best chance of succeeding, with the club attempting to juggle European competition and the league for the first time. The arrival of the Portugal centre-back António Silva, 22, from Benfica looks a typically smart replacement for Marcos Senesi, 29. Kroupi’s freak foot injury, which will probably keep him out until November, may have proved a blessing in disguise in terms of retaining the 20-year-old. BF

Avoiding a repeat of last year’s upheaval was a major boost. Keith Andrews held on to his best players and made smart additions to a solid squad. Mamadou Sangaré has added quality in midfield since joining from Lens and looks the bargain of the summer. Callum Wilson has brought experience up front after signing on a free and Jaidon Anthony provides cover on the flanks after his £15m move from Burnley. El Hadji-Malick Diouf, signed from West Ham, offers potential at left-back. Jacob Steinberg

Deadline day deals to bring in the exciting Nigeria forward Femi Azeez from Millwall and the Spanish midfielder Chema Andrés from Stuttgart made it 12 signings in another summer of transition, Azeez’s arrival being announced almost 12 hours after the window shut. The departures of Jan Paul van Hecke, Carlos Baleba and Carl Rushworth brought in more than £140m as the Brighton model continues to deliver big profits, although losing last season’s top scorer, Danny Welbeck, to Chelsea for a mere £5m may be the biggest loss if the new striker Promise David cannot bring the goals. Xabi Alonso’s appointment as manager was the biggest signing of the summer. Chelsea have been sensible since turning to the Spaniard. Morgan Rogers has started well after joining for £117m. Maxence Lacroix adds power in defence, Marco Palestra versatility on the flanks. Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson can raise standards in the dressing room. But there was the usual revolving door. It remains to be seen whether Coventry have struck the right balance in the market. Frank Lampard wanted to maintain momentum but add power and physicality. Coventry also sought to address their lack of Premier League experience with Taiwo Awoniyi and Ethan Pinnock. Coventry were the highest scorers in English football’s top four tiers last season but the step up means the pressure is on Awoniyi, never prolific for Nottingham Forest, Sidiki Cherif, a promising 19-year-old, and Ellis Simms to deliver before Haji Wright returns from injury. #866. Republic of Ireland talisman Parrott caps dream year with two more goals

Troy Parrott has scored 17 international goals in 43 caps

A year and a day on from his hat-trick in Budapest which helped Republic of Ireland snatch a dramatic 3-2 win over Hungary to make the World Cup play-offs, Troy Parrott scored another two big goals to help the Irish to a 3-0 win over Kosovo in the Nations League.

His two penalties set Heimir Hallgrimsson's side on their way to a much-needed victory as they secured second spot in Group B3 - which brings with it a place in pot two for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw and a Nations League play-off with the chance to go up to League A for the first time.

The two strikes brought Parrott's tally for his country up to 17 in 43 caps.

Twelve of those goals have come in his past nine competitive appearances, with six in his past three games at the Aviva Stadium.

The past 12 months have been transformative for Parrott, who also earned a move to Real Betis in the summer after starring for AZ Alkmaar.

He has since scored against Real Madrid and in the Champions League for Betis alongside establishing himself as Republic of Ireland's talisman.

He will carry their hopes of qualifying for Euro 2028, just as his idol and the country's all-time leading scorer Robbie Keane did for many years when he led the line.

While he has taken an arduous route to the top, Parrott is content he is finally fulfilling his potential at club level and on the international stage.

"Growing up watching Robbie Keane, he was the main man and it's always what I wanted to do. I've worked really hard to get here and now I'm in a really good spot," he told RTE.

"Professional football is one of the hardest professions to make it in, so many people want to be a footballer. If I didn't have a stronger mentality, I could have failed.

"Now I am at the level that I always knew I could get to and there are more levels to come. I am really excited for it."

Republic of Ireland seal second with win over 10-man Kosovo

Republic of Ireland finished their Nations League campaign with two wins, two draws and two defeats from their six games.

The two victories were highlights of what was a testing campaign on and off the pitch because of the decision to go ahead with two games against Israel.

The controversy surrounding the first Israel game in particular - which the Irish ended up winning 3-0 in Debrecen - was difficult for the squad to navigate.

The match looked in doubt the previous day when training was delayed as players took a vote on whether to play - amid protests over the Israel-Gaza war - with goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu making himself unavailable for selection.

Parrott reiterated the point that Dara O'Shea and Nathan Collins made earlier in the week, that the collective group of players are stronger coming out the other side of it all.

"It was very difficult the last camp with all the pressure on us as players, it was a bit of a strange one because no-one has experienced anything like that before - players, staff or the FAI - so it was strange and a bit difficult," he said.

"It was important for us because people had to come out of their shells and give opinions, the quiet ones had to have a voice in the changing room so it was good everyone came together.

"When we played Israel in the away game the performance symbolised everything we went through in the week, we came out and destroyed them."

Republic of Ireland will face a League A side in March's two-legged play-off for the chance to reach the top tier for the first time

Republic of Ireland had many "nearly" moments in the group, from the late narrow defeats in Pristina and Linz to the frustration of being pegged back by Israel and Austria in draws when they were ahead.

The pressure was on for them to deliver in their must-win game against Kosovo on Tuesday and they did, comfortably.

Although aided by the red card shown to Kreshnik Hajrizi, Parrott believes they would have still won had Kosovo had 11 men on the pitch and was relieved they could demonstrate again, as they did against Portugal and Hungary last year, that they can win when it matters.

Moving up to pot two for next month's Euro 2028 draw should, in theory, present the Irish with a kinder draw for a tournament they are desperate to qualify for, given the Aviva Stadium will host some games.

"We felt and everyone else felt we could have won this group but the most important thing is getting into that pot two. It was a big game for us, it wasn't a nearly game we went out and done it so it's a credit to everyone.

"It's disappointing we didn't win the group because that's what we wanted to do at the start. There's been so many nearly matches where we have nearly won or played well and haven't won and I think tonight we went out there with the mindset no matter what, we had to win.

"It's not guaranteed that we will qualify [for the Euros] so it was important to get pot two to get a better draw and we'll be going to the qualifiers hoping to qualify. A tournament hosted by Ireland without Ireland in it would be heart-breaking, so that's our mission to make sure we're there."

Before attentions turns to Euro 2028 qualifying, Republic of Ireland will take on a League A side over two legs in March's Nations League play-off as they try to reach the top tier for the first time.

Parrott's focus between now and March is clear, getting back to Seville and "putting the ball in the back of the net" for Real Betis as he has done so well for Republic of Ireland in the past year.

#864. Can global leaders put their money where their mouth is on climate?

World leaders warn that geopolitical divisions are distracting from the climate crisis as negotiations focus on clean energy and financing, while Iran calls for compensation for war-related environmental damage.

The slow international response to climate change has placed the world on a path to destruction, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres told heads of state and government during opening statements at this year's COP31 climate conference.

"The ⁠brutal truth is that the climate crisis is outrunning us," he said, as world leaders gathered in the Turkish resort city of Antalya to set the tone for negotiations at the UN climate summit.

A UN reportlast month found ​the world will cross a temperature threshold countries agreed to pursue in order to prevent runaway global heating. At the same time, states like Germany are slipping down the rankings for climate action, according to the annual Climate Change Performance Index published Wednesday by New Climate Institute and Germanwatch.

Nonetheless, Guterres said the world has "the power to make sure the overshoot is a temporary breach."

Negotiators from close to 200 countries are meeting in Turkey at the end of a year characterized by extreme heat waves and a glacier collapse in Nepal that triggered a flood, killing more than 1,400 people and leaving thousands more missing.

At this year's talks, national representatives are discussing climate solutions such as increasing the share of electricity in an effort to move away from fossil fuels.

On Thursday, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, one of the few heads of government from Europe's major economies attending the summit, said that the world's dependence on fossil fuels was at the heart of both the climate crisis and energy security challenges.

"The shift to clean energy is the only route to energy security," he said, endorsing the conference's focus on electrification which he said would lower energy bills, create jobs and protect people from the volatility of fossil fuel markets.

Burnham promised a "new era of British leadership over the next decade," announcing the UK would put climate resilience high on the agenda during its G20 presidency next year.

The US, the world's largest historical emitter of damaging greenhouse gases, is not attending the summit — for the second year in a row after US President Donald Trump withdrew the country from the Paris Agreement in 2025.

Other nations, including big polluters like Germany, France, Italy, Canada and Japan, also opted not to send their top leaders to the talks.

On Wednesday, Turkey's President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, who is hosting COP31 together with Australia, which is leading negotiations, called on developed nations to take greater responsibility on climate finance.

Financing disagreements center around who should pay for international climate action, whether funding should take the form of grants or loans and how to scale monetary support for developing nations. Many of these countries are among the most vulnerable to the climate crisis but have contributed very little to the emissions causing it.

Erdogan said while previous conferences had resulted in different ideas around financing, they have yet to be turned into action. "We set out to make this an implementation COP," he told leaders.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen addressed remarks that developed nations are not contributing enough to climate finance, saying that the transition away from fossil fuels is in "our common interest."

"Europe is the world's largest provider of climate finance. Last year alone, we contributed more than €32 billion [about $35.5 billion] to support developing countries," she said, adding that Europe will continue to support partners worldwide in tackling climate change.

A recent Carbon Brief analysis found that public funding pledged under the Paris Agreement to help developing countries tackle climate change fell by more than 70% in 2026.

Most multi-year pledges from donor countries expired in 2025. Since then, the US has stepped back from international climate efforts, while several European countries have cut their aid budgets, reported Carbon Brief.

Hilda Heine, president of the Marshall Islands in the Pacific, which face an existential threat from rising sea levels, said the response to overshoot "must be overwhelming" and quickly reversed otherwise "the world we know is over."

"Every fraction of a degree of warming brings more catastrophe," said Heine, adding that more warming makes it more difficult to adapt to living on a hotter planet, brings greater loss and damage from worsening weather extremes and greater financial need.

She called on leaders to triple climate finance by 2035 and make it easier for Small Island Developing States to access the money.

"We are told there is no money, but their spending on war grows; the greatest security threat we face remains underfunded. I appeal to you: Find money for life, not death. Replenish the climate funds," Heine said.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese spoke of a "solemn responsibility to this and to future generations ​to act," adding that this is the critical decade.

Australia, the world's third-largest fossil fuel exporter, has vowed to promote the views of the "Pacific family" — small Pacific nations in the region such as Tuvalu or Fiji, where pre-COP meetings were held in October.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Albanese said it was crucial that climate cooperation delivered practical results — "unlocking investment in clean energy technologies, accelerating electrification, speeding up action for our oceans, unlocking climate finance for those who need it ​most."

As reasons to speed up electrification von der Leyen pointed to wildfires in Europe and floods in Nepal, as well as droughts stretching from Central America to Sudan, and to the disruption to energy supplies linked to the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz.

"The world is witnessing the cost of continuing with the status quo for our climate and our energy security," she said, adding that the European Union would double down on efforts to become climate neutral.

"Three-quarters ​of humanity live in countries that import fossil fuels, hostage to price shocks they did ​not create and cannot ‌control," UN Secretary-General Guterres said, adding that recent conflicts have made clear a shift to renewable energy would help improve energy security and the cost-of-living crisis.

Von der Leyen also expressed support for COP31's 35-by-35 electrification pledge. The pledge aims to increase electricity's share of final global energy use to 35% by 2035, with von der Leyen saying Europe would be the first "electro-powered" continent.

Heine of the Marshall Islands said electrification must must be strictly tied to renewable energy generation rather than fossil fuels, warning that continued oil, coal and gas extraction was a threat to her country's survival.

Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian said his country wanted compensation for environmental damage caused by US and Israeli strikes, including oil leaks from attacks on tankers. The strikes began in February.

Iran, which is a major fossil fuel producer and has pushed back against strict language on phasing out oil and gas at previous COPs alongside other petrostates, has also struck tankers in the Strait of Hormuz.

Pezeshkian linked the issue to climate finance and said his country expected "responsibility in times of war, to document and assess the environmental damages caused by military aggressions and to develop compensation mechanisms."

Brazil's President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who hosted last year's COP in the Amazonian city of Belem, said the momentum for climate action had dropped off at the start of the year, partly due to the Iran war.

"We started talking more about weapons and tariffs than the survival ‌of future generations," he said.

He also warned that "climate agreements are the favorite targets of reactionary forces at COPs," and urged leaders to work together. Lula promised to protect the Amazon rainforest. "Brazil is back to defend the continuity of a healthy planet," he said.

This article was last updated on November 12 to reflect incoming statements from world leaders.

#863. Bellamy convinced of Wales credentials despite defeat by Portugal

Craig Bellamy's Wales seriously tested reigning Nations League champions Portugal in Cardiff

Craig Bellamy kept coming back to one word. Belief.

His Wales side had just lost a fifth game out of six to finish bottom of their Nations League group. Bellamy would have been forgiven for feeling a little bruised.

But there are ways of losing and ways of finishing bottom.

Wales were fearless against Portugal, exhilarating in attack and proving they can compete at the highest level of this competition, even as they were beaten 3-2 in Cardiff.

And while they were already consigned to the foot of the Group A4 table, Wales' previous performances mean they at least have the back-up of a relegation play-off in March to preserve their top-flight status.

"Belief's the biggest one," Bellamy said when he was asked what he and his team had taken from this campaign.

"Not just this game, but in general. We are beyond close to this level. We can more than compete at this level.

"We demand and want to expect to be. Getting into League A is big for us, but also staying in A is going to allow us to develop.

"You can only develop and improve by playing the best teams, and I felt we've taken another shift."

Portugal hold off bold Wales in five-goal thriller

Former Wales captain Craig Bellamy was appointed head coach in July 2024

Wales have certainly fared better than they did when they were last in the top tier of the Nations League, when they finished with one point from six games and were relegated.

Victory against World Cup quarter-finalists Norway last month was their first at this level and, had they been more clinical in Oslo on Saturday, they might have got a second win of the campaign.

Ultimately, Wales' inability to take their chances â combined with sloppy defensive mistakes â meant their results did not match their performances.

And the reality is that they were up against stellar opposition, whose vastly superior resources showed with their greater ruthlessness at both ends of the pitch.

"If there's anything you would have learned from these games, then you see killers. That's why they're at the top," Bellamy added.

"I know people look at results. I'm fully aware of the business. This is all I know. But I think when you look at reality as well, and you look at our performances during this group, I couldn't ask for more.

"I feel we're closer than probably maybe the players thought they were. It's fine margins.

"But I feel the biggest word out of this now has been belief, really, for me."

Highlights: 10-man Portugal defeat Wales to top Nations League group

Wales had the best record of the four teams who finished bottom of their top-flight groups, meaning they have a second chance to avoid relegation in the form of a two-leg play-off in March.

At Friday's draw in Switzerland, Bellamy's side will discover whether they will face Slovenia, Hungary, Republic of Ireland or Bosnia-Herzegovina, who beat them in a World Cup play-off earlier this year.

Those teams all finished second in their League B groups and, as the League A team, Wales will have home advantage in the second leg.

"Going into the next one, we have to be in this group," said Bellamy. "If we want to develop as a football nation and keep going forward, we have to be playing against the best teams. It's only going to improve you.

"I know we can go back to League B... It's about playing the best teams. That's how we're going to get better. I honestly believe it."

Bellamy, who has a contract running to 2028, said: "I won't be here for the next Nations League. I won't be the manager then. So I'm doing it for the next one, but I'm also doing it for the players.

"We've got to. That's how we're going to be the best version of us and keep improving."

#861. Jennifer Lopez Addresses "Disappointing" Divorce From Ben Affleck

Nearly two years after Jennifer Lopez and Ben Affleck finalized their divorce, the "Let's Get Loud" singer looked back at the aftermath of their "disappointing" breakup.

Jennifer Lopez knows that sometimes, love does cost a thing.

Nearly two years after the "On The Floor" singer and Ben Affleck finalized their divorce, she reflected on the weight of their breakup—and whether she's ready to dance again with someone new.

"I'm done with that part of my life," Lopez said on the Nov. 17 episode of Benny Blanco and Lil Dicky's Friends Keep Secrets podcast. "It was such a hard, disappointing last situation on every level. On every level, it was so disappointing. I don't ever want to delve into that."

Though she is focusing on living life single, that doesn't mean she'll never be ready for another great love story, especially after taking a deeper look at her split from the Oscar winner.

"I'm OK with myself," she explained. "I was a serial monogamist, one after the other, trying to find the thing, hoping that this was it."

Now, the 57-year-old—mom to 18-year-old twins Max and Emme with ex-husband Marc Anthony—is getting loud with advice for others navigating divorce.

"Always operate in a way that you'll feel proud of when you look back," she shared. Looking back at her experiences, she added, "Even as painful as some of them were so bad—life-shifting pain and hurt—I can look back and be like, 'I loved completely. I acted in a way that I was proud of as a human. I didn't treat anybody in any way that I would be ashamed of.'"

"I did the best that I could in the moment with what I knew," she continued. "That's my advice for anything because when you go through hard things like that, it's easy to be like, 'F--k this.' You're in so much pain you want to hurt somebody else, or somebody has hurt you so much, but you can't. I've always held myself to that kind of standard."

Since then, Lopez—who filed for divorce from Affleck in August 2024, exactly two years after they got married—has continued to carry what she learned from their breakup and its aftermath.

"Be the best person that you can be right now, every single time, especially when it's hard," she emphasized. "When you say you're strong, I think that's part of it. I can look at these things and be like, 'It's OK. These are experiences in my journey.'"

"I don't know why it was my journey sometimes," she admitted. "Then I realized, no, I'm here to learn something. I finally got to a place where I feel like I've learned it, but it took the f--king house to fall down on top of me to do that."

Looking ahead, the "Let's Get Loud" singer—who was first engaged to Affleck in 2002 before splitting two years later—will be dancing for her papi when the time is right.

"I'm different," she said. "Because it changed me. Because I allowed it to change me. Because I wanted to learn the thing. I was like, 'It's done. I'm not doing this anymore. What are you going to do different?'"

"You can intellectually be a smart person and know things," she explained. "But the knowing is not the thing. It's changing the behavior and the patterns. That's the thing. And that is a conscious action that you have to do. You have to change."

#860. Belief and bench steer Northern Ireland into Nations League top tier

Highlights: Northern Ireland secure to promotion to League A

After going 500 minutes without conceding a goal, Northern Ireland could be forgiven for having to make adjustments to play from behind.

Having travelled to Budapest knowing a point against Hungary would be enough to top Nations League B2, Barnabas Varga's strike after 35 minutes for the hosts at the Puskas Arena altered the picture and, for the first time in the campaign, left Michael O'Neill's side having to chase a game.

Their response to the deficit - on the pitch, from the bench and high in the stands where their suspended manager was watching the game - displayed the best characteristics of a side who had not won at this level before this unbeaten campaign.

While the point from a 1-1 draw in Budapest will be long remembered for Justin Devenny's brilliant equaliser and the scenes of celebration that greeted promotion to the competition's top tier for the first time, it was beyond the highlights and headlines that O'Neill saw the emerging qualities of his side.

"We went behind tonight and it was difficult, you know? Big stadium, big atmosphere, but we came out and played well in the second half and got what we needed from the game," said the manager.

"Those are things that I'm very pleased that are in this squad at such a young age. The technical side of the game we'll always look to improve on, but in terms of the physical, the tactical and the mental side of a game, we're very far ahead of where I thought we would be at this time."

Northern Ireland draw with Hungary to seal Nations League promotion

Watch: Devenny the hero as NI earn promotion

Hungary enjoyed more than 70% possession in the first half, and they could have been further than a goal ahead with Liverpool star Dominik Szoboszlai striking the base of the post after only five minutes.

O'Neill made his first change at half-time, bringing on veteran striker Josh Magennis, while Kieran Morrison, Brodie Spencer and Paul Smyth all followed in the second half.

Magennis and Morrison made a real impact before the equaliser, but it was the belief shown by all involved that O'Neill felt was key to the turnaround.

"I felt in the first half from where I was seeing the game, we just looked a little bit leggy which is natural," added O'Neill.

"I just felt we needed that freshness at the right points in the game that helped us, but it was the belief that we could get back into the game, and the belief that we could see the game out.

"I think we showed a lot of attributes that are in this squad at this moment in time and certainly in the second half that was that was the case."

'I genuinely believe it will only get better' - O'Neill

For all the plaudits earned by this team who conceded just one goal in six games while picking up 12 points, among the most impressive aspects of the campaign has been who they have had to do without.

Talismanic Liverpool defender Conor Bradley has not played for this side in over 12 months through injury.

Ali McCann is another who missed both 2026 Nations League windows, while influential defender Daniel Ballard featured only in the first game in Georgia before a hamstring injury.

Arsenal's Ceadach O'Neill was forced to pull out of the November squad through injury at a time when he would perhaps have been the most natural replacement for Jamie Donley after the striker picked up a second booking against Ukraine last week and had to miss the finale through suspension.

Having taken over an ageing squad four years ago, O'Neill has rebuilt his playing panel with a group that feels as if it is getting deeper with each international window.

"The encouraging thing is we have players on the outside - we've Bradley to come back in, Ballard to come back in, Ali McCann, young Ceadach, Eoin Toal," added the former Stoke City and Blackburn Rovers boss.

"We have good competition for places now. We're going to need that competition, and some players are going to miss out, but we are building depth to the squad that will help us going forward."

Come the next Nations League, that will be all the way into the uncharted territory of the top tier.

#859. Isaiah Washington Debuts New Romance One Year After Wife’s Death

Grey’s Anatomy alum Isaiah Washington revealed he’s in a new relationship with content creator Kei Bennett one year after his wife Jenisa Garland’s death: “She is all mine now and I am all hers."

It’s a beautiful day for Isaiah Washington’s personal life.

More than a year after the Grey’s Anatomy alum shared wife Jenisa Garland had died suddenly in June 2025, he detailed his next chapter with content creator Kei Bennett.

“I have known many incredible women in my life,” Washington wrote on Instagram Nov. 17 alongside a photo of the new lady in his life, “but not a single one of them can hold a candle to the deep Southern charm of @keibenet.”

“I am not only thrilled to have gotten to know her in the last 9 months talking to her for hours every single day,” he wrote, “I am absolutely baffled how any man in her past could have harmed her, belittled her, disrespected her, or even betrayed her in the most deplorable ways.”

As for how she’s pulled at his heart strings?

“She has an incredible mind, heart, and spirit and I have grown to respect her intelligence, green thumb, hair stylist talent, entrepreneurship, holistic approach, and her black business owner's business acumen immensely,” he explained. “Yes, she has earned her place at my creative table and I love her dearly.”

And while Bennett may have kissed her fair share of frogs in the past, he feels they were all leading to her prince.

“I am so glad that all of the men who treated her like she was less than a Queen, all left her heartbroken, but not broken,” he wrote. “Don’t worry I will take it from here and I will never let her down as a friend and partner in love and creativity.”

“There has been no other woman who has made me laugh and has encouraged me as she has,” he added. “Yeah, I don't play about Kei Bennett, and just know that she doesn't play about me. Yeah…she is all mine now and I am all hers. Deal with it.”

And it’s clear Bennett is just as smitten, commenting under the post, “I love you to pieces. Thank you for this. My protector, my best friends, my love, Mousie’s poppop…you exceed every goal you set and have the most pure heart I’ve ever seen.”

The couple’s hard launch comes after Washington’s wife of 29 years died following a weeklong health battle in June 2025. Just last month, he shared deeper insight into the tragedy.

"It came as a huge shock to me and our entire family," Washington—dad to kids Isaiah, Tyme and Iman with Garland—captioned his Oct. 3 Instagram post. "She succumbed to a massive hemorrhagic stroke and never recovered."

And while her death came as a shock to their family, Washington shared how grateful he was to have his three kids by his side during the devastating chapter. As he put it, "She has been gone 16 months now, but she left 3 incredibly amazing children behind to continue her legacy."

For a closer look into the love lives of more Grey’s Anatomy stars, keep reading…

After being introduced in 1995, Isaiah Washington knew pretty quickly that he wanted to scrub in with Jenisa Garland, the two tying the knot one year later.

"For me, being married and having children did change a lot of my trajectory," the actor, who starred as renowned cardiothoracic surgeon Preston Burke for three seasons of Grey's Anatomy, told Fox News Digital in 2022. "That's why I didn't want to get married 25 years ago, but I'm glad I did because the wife and children really make you the best human being that you can be."

Sadly, their 29-year marriage came to an untimely end when Garland—who shared kids Isaiah, Tyme and Iman with Washington—passed away in 2025.

"It came as a huge shock to me and our entire family," Washington wrote in an October 2026 Instagram post. "She succumbed to a massive hemorrhagic stroke and never recovered."

But more than a year after the tragedy, Washington found love again with content creator Kei Bennett.

“She has an incredible mind, heart, and spirit and I have grown to respect her intelligence, green thumb, hair stylist talent, entrepreneurship, holistic approach, and her black business owner's business acumen immensely,” he explained in a November 2026 social media post. “Yes, she has earned her place at my creative table and I love her dearly.”

Looks like it was record producer Chris Ivery who asked series lead Ellen Pompeo to pick me, choose me, love me after they crossed paths at a Los Angeles grocery store in 2003.

"I was with my mutual friend," the actress—who's starred as Meredith Grey since the series' 2005 premiere—detailed during a 2022 appearance on The Drew Barrymore Show.

So, after sharing a quick hello with her fellow Boston-area native, "He called me a bunch of times, and I wouldn't call him back. And then he said, 'You're rude. You won't call me back,' and I said, 'Well, because I'm not trying to go on a date with you.' And he said, 'Who's trying to go on a date with you? I don't even know you.'"

Basically, she continued, "We had a fight first. That's kind of always the way to my heart, is like, piss me off and I'm all yours."

Married four years later, the pair welcomed daughter Stella in 2009, her little sister Sienna in 2014 and son Christopher in 2016.

"We're sort of two kids who made it out and then landed in Hollywood and jumped on this ride," Pompeo said of their journey during a 2025 appearance on Alex Cooper's Call Her Daddy podcast. "We just couldn't believe that something was actually happening—that it was great, that I had this great job and we were getting to travel all over the world."

James Pickens Jr.'s starting line with wife Gina Taylor-Pickens dates back to the 1980s when the then-struggling actors met through the New York City theater scene. "I thought she was cute," the future chief medical officer Richard Webber explained to TV Fanatic, "and she gave me her number."

A stroll through Central Park proved to be the first steps of their forever. "We have a mantra that we've lived by for 35 years," the dad to Carl and Gavyn explained of the Deliver Us from Eva actress on a 2019 episode of Live with Kelly and Ryan. "Love unconditionally, forgive quickly and treat strife and trouble like a basket of rattlesnakes."

The romance between E.R. Fightmaster's neuroscientist Kai Bartley and Caterina Scorsone's neurosurgeon Amelia Shepherd may have been cut short during season 19, but as a wise woman once said, "If you aren’t willing to keep looking for light in the darkest of places without stopping, even when it seems impossible, you will never succeed."

And the skies certainly seemed sunny as Scorsone (mom to daughters Eliza, Pippa and Arwen with ex-husband Rob Giles) and Fightmaster strolled through L.A. in March 2026. Holding hands as they exited local mini-chain Highly Likely it seemed, uh, pretty certain that they were a couple.

While Ben Warren has switched in and out of scrubs as anesthesiologist turned firefighter turned surgical resident, Jason George, who starred on Grey's and its spin-off Station 19, has never wavered in his committment to writer wife Vandana Khanna.

Meeting at the University of Virginia, "She's my day one," he raved to Us Weekly of his bride, mom to Jasmine, Nikhil and Arun. "I've known this woman since before I knew I wanted to be an actor. I’ve known her over half my life. I’ve known her longer than I haven’t known her."

He shared his prescription for a decades-long union during a 2017 appearance on Steve Harvey's titular talk show.

"You're gonna have fights, because if you don't have fights, you're not being honest," he noted, stressing the importance of fighting fair. "When you settle it, don't say it's settled if it's not, and then bring it up again six months later."

Following marriages to Jane Parker and Arielle Goldrath, Kevin McKidd (a.k.a. army vet and recently departed head of trauma Owen Hunt) debuted a real-life crossover in November 2023, making his red carpet debut with Station 19 star Danielle Savre at the Global Down Syndrome Foundation's 15th Annual Be Beautiful Be Yourself Fashion Show.

The pairing "just kind of happened," the dad of four explained to People months later at The Walt Disney Company’s 2023 Emmy Awards Celebration. "We're really happy and she's an amazing human being, so I feel lucky on many levels in my life right now."

Crossing paths with French filmmaker Manu Boyer at a New York swimming pool, Kim Raver decided to fully dive in. "That first meeting is kind of sacred," she detailed to Women's Health in 2005, "so I think I want to keep it to myself."

Though she was willing to share how her husband—the two share sons Luke and Leo—helped her prepare for cardiothoracic surgeon Teddy Altman's first intimate encounter with onscreen love Cass Beckman (Sophia Bush).

With Raver also tasked with directing the scene, "I couldn't tell whether he was like, 'This is awesome,' or, 'Wait, how are you going to do this?'" she admitted to People. "And I was like, 'This is how we're going to do it.'"

Camilla Luddington and Matthew Alan's first date to a 2008 The Temper Trap concert proved to be a moment, a love, a dream, aloud. Because 11 years after that initial outing—and two after the actors welcomed their daughter Hayden in 2017—they wed in front of 70 loved ones in Santa Barbara, Calif., with Luddington walking down the aisle to the band's hit "Sweet Disposition."

As the British star, who's embodied general surgeon-turned OB/GYN resident Dr. Jo Wilson since 2012, put it to People at the time, "We're just ready to do the damn thing. Chris Carmack has unique insight on how his orthopedic surgeon Atticus "Link" Lincoln fell for longtime friend Jo. (The concert violinist, touring fiddler and vocalist appeared on the series as a backup singer and also played in series star Sam Palladio's band.)

"We met, maybe there was some attraction, it didn't make sense at the time," Slaver explained in a March 2026 video on their YouTube channel. Agreed Carmack, in a relationship at the time, "You were off-limits for me for a minute."

After they "floated around in the same circles for a year," noted Carmack, they started dating, marrying in 2018, two years after they welcomed daughter Kai. Youngest daughter Cielle joined the band in 2022.

Since 1984, Debbie Allen has been huddled up with former NBA point guard Norm Nixon. But the pair didn't become instant teammates after meeting on the set of The Fish That Saved Pittsburgh in 1979.

"She went to New York and moved to Fame, and I went back to Los Angeles," the athlete recounted to Trib Total Media. "We stayed in touch, and I realized I had more fun with her than any of the other women I was dating."

As the Debbie Allen Dance Academy founder—who's appeared as world-class urologist and board chairman Catherine Fox since 2011—put it, they're usually in sync.

"I think our relationship has always been born on friendship and commonality in terms of things that we both like," the mom to Vivian, Norman Jr. and Nixon's son DeVaughn told People in 2024, noting they both like "to read books. We both like to go to the movies. We both like to travel. We both love our children."

Decades in, "We've hit some rocks and hit some walls," she acknowledged. "But at the end of the day, we really love each other and we sleep together every night and we love our family."

Safe to say Harry Shum Jr.'s first date with now-wife Shelby Rabara was a dream.

"We both cried and it was just such a beautiful experience because after that we just talked about you," he told Jennifer Hudson during a 2022 appearance on her talk show of their Dreamgirls viewing. "It really kinda brought us together and we opened up about a lot of things and it was just such a beautiful first date."

Naturally, there was no way they could ever go. The Glee alum (who plays recently fired resident Benson Kwan) and the Steven Universe star wed in November 2015, welcoming daughter Xia four years later.

Transplant surgeon Nick Marsh has proven to be Meredith's person since entering the Grey's universe in 2018. But off-camera it's fiancée Lindsay Rae Hofmann who's stolen Speedman's heart.

Engaged since 2023, the Felicity alum and the co-founder of swimwear brand Juillet welcomed daughter Pfeiffer in 2021 and son Indy in 2024. And she's provided quite the assist to his growing television career.

"She started watching You, and then I ended up on that show," he explained to Esquire in 2021. "She started binge-watching Grey's Anatomy on Netflix during the pandemic, and here I am. Whatever she seems to watch, I seem to end up on."

#857. A new view of Amazonian leaf seasonality

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Gerbrand Koren is at the Copernicus Institute of Sustainable Development, Utrecht University, 3584 CB Utrecht, the Netherlands.

The Amazon rainforest plays a key part in the cycling of carbon and water on regional and global scales, and is widely viewed as a perennially evergreen ecosystem. However, writing in Nature, Song et al.1 report that there are extended periods when trees in most of the rainforest remain leafless. Known as deciduousness, this state occurs between the shedding of old leaves and the emergence and early development (flushing) of fresh ones. The authors also found that hydroclimatic conditions such as annual rainfall have a more crucial role in determining this pattern of leaf behaviour than do soil properties and light availability. The seasonal variation in tropical leaf cover and photosynthetic activity in the Amazon observed by the authors is less pronounced than that seen for broadleaf trees in temperate and boreal climate zones.

#856. Joe Jonas Reveals Cheeky Gift He Recently Gave Ex Demi Lovato

Joe Jonas recently revealed that he gave Demi Lovato, whom he dated briefly in 2010, a cheeky birthday gift that nodded toward one of her most viral interview moments.

Joe Jonas’ favorite meme? He would have to say mug.

More than 10 years after Demi Lovato went viral for revealing mugs were her “favorite dish” during an interview with NRJ Berlin, her Camp Rock costar—whom she dated briefly in 2010—revealed it’s still his favorite pop culture moment.

“It’s amazing,” Joe told his brothers Kevin Jonas and Nick Jonas during the Nov. 17 episode of their Hey Jonas! podcast. “I bought her a mug as a gift for coming as our special guest recently or her birthday. I think I sent her a mug for her birthday. I can’t remember.”

Meanwhile, Kevin and Joe agreed it was a great clip.  As Kevin emphasized, “She wasn’t incorrect.”

For Demi’s part, she recently revealed that she intentionally had misinterpreted the question—the interviewer was referring to food rather than cookware—but she opted to answer it in her own way.

“I had been asked so many questions that day,” Demi reflected during an appearance on Keke Palmer’s Baby, It’s Keke Palmer podcast in March. “I was doing, like, a press tour and you get bored doing press tours.”

And so, the Disney Channel alum joked she thought at the time, “‘I’m gonna start f--king with the interviewers.’”

“I just ran with it,” Demi joked, emphasizing that only part of the interview went viral. “In the long, extended video, you see me look at my tour manager and like smirk. Like, ‘did you catch that one?’ And then that went viral and everyone thought I was serious.”

But there’s nothing wrong with being confident in answering the question this way, especially given Demi made a worthy case for mugs.

“I like mugs because they’re very comfortable in your hand,” she said in the now-viral clip. “And they hold hot things that you don’t have to touch. So, you know, coffee or hot tea.”

As for Joe running so far with the joke that he sent his ex a mug as a present? While Demi previously joked she was “mad” at Joe following their breakup, there’s no longer any mean mugging between them.

“It’s been such a wonderful relationship through so many years,” Joe told USA Today earlier this year after he and Demi each made appearances at each other’s respective concerts. “I feel so grateful that Demi and I can go perform together still and see each other in these different journeys of our life.”

For more Disney alums who dated, keep reading…

Disney Channel worlds collided after Sabrina Carpenter met Bradley Steven Perry.

The Girl Meets World star and Good Luck Charlie actor’s romance began in 2014, when Carpenter’s show began filming right next door to Perry’s Mighty Med.

“[It was a] really unique way to ask someone out,” Carpenter told J-14 at the time, describing a scene out of a pirate flick: “Like, they do the little bottles and they put notes in them and send them across the ocean, like one of those, and [he] put a note inside. It was cute.”

Though they broke up in 2015, Perry—who married Candace Cameron Bure’s daughter Natasha Bure in 2025—noted that their connection was a sweet young love.

“Sabrina was my first girlfriend,” Perry said during an appearance on the Unplanned Podcast in 2024. “We dated for about two years.”

He added, “It was very much like a little high school relationship.”

Bella Thorne and Gregg Sulkin shook up young Hollywood when they first stepped out together in 2015.

But the Shake It Up alum and Wizards of Waverly Place actor went their separate ways a year later.

“Our schedules made seeing each other difficult," Thorne and Sulkin told People in a joint statement back in 2016, “and we decided that for now this would be best.”

But they’ll always look back on their fairytale romance with a smile.

“After much thought and soul-searching, we have made the difficult decision to end our relationship,” they added. “We will always love each other and have a deep respect for one another, as we have each grown to be better people because of our time together.”

Can you imagine what would happen if Zac Efron and Vanessa Hudgens never dated?

The High School Musical alums hit it off as soon as the cameras started rolling for the franchise’s first film in 2005.

“We created a bond right from the start,” Hudgens—who played the Gabriella Montez to Efron’s Troy Bolton in the films—told People in 2022. “We were like, ‘We’re doing this, it’s us or nothing.’”

“It started off really organically,” she added. “I could not have been more grateful to have that relationship at that time.”

And while the pair eventually had to go their own ways, you can still bet on the fact that they had a next-level connection.

As Hudgens put it on a 2025 episode of Bart Johnson's Get Your Head In The Game podcast, "Of course I was a child and paired with this boy and I was like, 'Oh my god, he's so cute.' The chemistry was so real."

Nick Jonas and Selena Gomez’s romance was burnin’ up from 2008 to 2010.

And while they shared two years together, Gomez’s real prize from the relationship would have to be her unbreakable bond with BFF Taylor Swift.”

“Taylor and I dated the Jonas Brothers,” Gomez—who married Benny Blanco in 2025—said during a 2025 episode of the Therapuss with Jake Shane podcast of how she and Swift met. “I dated Nick and she dated Joe [Jonas]. And everything  was cute, we were young. We all know and love each other now and it’s so cute.”

Gomez added of her relationship with Jonas, dad to daughter Malti with wife Priyanka Chopra, “She and I like to say the best thing we got out of those relationships was each other because it was really sweet.”

At one point, Miley Cyrus thought Dylan Sprouse could be the one.

Indeed, the Hannah Montana alum revealed she and The Suite Life of Zack & Cody star were much more than work colleagues.

“Dylan Sprouse was my boyfriend,” Cyrus told Alex Cooper during the March 2026 Disney+ Hannah Montana 20th Anniversary Special. “I think he was the cutest.”

Responding to past rumors that she and Sprouse—who married model Barbara Palvin in 2023—were an item, the “Flowers” singer added, “It's true, confirmed.”

But during their brief romance, she also got to spend quality time with Sprouse’s twin brother Cole Sprouse—though she knew she couldn’t have the best of both worlds.

“Dylan was my crush,” Cyrus continued. “Their dad would take us to sushi. I was into the whole culture, and it was a two-for-one. Like, bring the brother. Hello!”

Joe Jonas and Demi Lovato may be like Venus and Mars, but they were once on the same astral plane.

After all, the Camp Rock alums took their romance offscreen in 2010 while filming the film’s sequel, though they backed down from the connection about a year later.

“Demi and I knew going into our romantic relationship that it may not be an easy one,” Jonas told Us Weekly in 2025. “I realize over the time we have shared together that I feel I care more about our friendship right now.”

That’s why the Jonas Brothers member wouldn’t change a thing about the love story he shared with Lovato—who married Jordan “Jutes” Lutes in 2025.

“It was my choice to break up,” Jonas—who shares daughters Willa and Delphine with ex-wife Sophie Turner—added, “but I love her as a friend. She’s been there for me when I needed her. I will continue to be her friend and be there for her.”

#855. Wael Mohya could make German football history at 17

At just 17, Gladbach forward Wael Mohya has earned his first Germany call-up. The dual-national talent has chosen the DFB path for now — and could soon make modern national-team history.

If you watch the Bundesliga, then you'll know Wael Mohya is a fast-footed, quick-thinking footballer. But not even the 17-year-old (Mohya turns 18 on December 31) Borussia Mönchengladbach youngster would have expected to be called up to the Germany squad so soon.

"Of course, I was absolutely thrilled. It means a great, great deal to me. I think everyone dreams of being selected for the national team at some point," Mohya said.

"And the fact that it's come to this now is, of course, just awesome and makes me very proud."

Mohya was at the gym when the call came in. He then shared the good news with his parents over dinner. "They started crying," the teenager said in a video posted on Gladbach's social media channels.

The youngster, who was born in a small town east of Düsseldorf, smiles and laughs a lot in interviews. He is always friendly, and in a good mood. On the field, too, he exudes the lightheartedness and carefree spirit of a 17-year-old.

As a technically skilled and creative player, Mohya often seeks out one-on-one situations and puts his opponents under pressure with quick dribbles. In nine Bundesliga appearances this season, Mohya has scored twice and delivered one assist.

"He's so cool and just plays really well. It's fun to watch him," Borussia coach Alexander Blessin said recently.

"Wael brings a lot to the team with his laid-back attitude on the field. He's not afraid to take risks, no matter how much pressure there is," added Gladbach's sporting director Rouven Schröder at a talk show on Sport1.

Borussia Mönchengladbach has been Mohya's sporting home since he was seven years old. Last season, previous head coach Eugen Polanski promoted him to the first team, and in December 2025, Mohya made his Bundesliga debut. Against Wolfsburg, aged 16 years and 347 days old, he became the youngest Bundesliga player in the club's history.

Mohya also recently completed a voluntary social year at an elementary school in Mönchengladbach. This is a program in Germany for young people who volunteer in the social sector — at hospitals, schools, or nursing homes, for example — for about six to 18 months. They gain work experience, help others, and earn a little money.

At the school's open all-day care program, Mohya helped serve meals, assisted children with their homework, and played with them. That's also where his nickname comes from. Because a girl hadn't understood his first name correctly or couldn't pronounce it, she called him "Waffel." Now, that name has stuck.

Even before being called up to the Germany team, clubs in the Bundesliga and across Europe's top leagues had taken notice of Mohya and were trying to sign him. His contract with Borussia Mönchengladbach runs through 2028.

With Gladbach currently in a relegation battle, his future appears likely to be elsewhere. If the club wants to generate transfer revenue from its biggest talent, next summer would likely be the opportunity to sell him — unless he extends his contract with Borussia.

The 17-year-old's career is managed by his parents. Whichever club can convince them that their son is in good hands and help him reach his full potential likely has the best chance of securing Mohya's signing.

Mohya himself says he doesn't even know how much he's currently earning at Gladbach.

"My parents take care of all that," he told Bild recently. "I get a monthly allowance, which is more than enough for me."

Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp recently revealed how much he had enjoyed his conversations with the youngster.

"The conversations I had with him were great," Klopp said with a laugh. "I wasn't that confident at 17, but then again, I wasn't that good either."

Since Mohya's parents are from Morocco, their son also holds Moroccan citizenship. As a result, he could have played for Morocco, but he has now decided against it. In fact, the Moroccan football association had been actively courting Mohya as early as last year and had already reached out to him in the run-up to the 2026 World Cup.

Now, like Frankfurt's Younes Ebnoutalib, Mohya will continue to play in the German jersey, unlike Schalke's Soufiane El-Faouzi, who chose Morocco, or Bayer Leverkusen's Ibrahim Maza, who likely would have been selected by Klopp as well if he hadn't already opted for Algeria.

For Mohya, who played for Germany's youth teams from the U16s through to the U21s, the door to Morocco remains open, even if he does play for Germany. According to FIFA regulations, players under the age of 21 can change national teams before their fourth international match (whether a competitive or friendly match), provided that none of those matches take place during a World Cup or a continental tournament such as the European Championship, Copa America, or Africa Cup of Nations.

If Mohya plays in the upcoming UEFA Nations League games in Serbia or against the Netherlands, another record is on the horizon. Although there were two even younger players who made their debuts in the Germany jersey — Willy Baumgärtner in 1908 (at 17 years and 104 days) and Marius Hiller in 1910 (at 17 years and 241 days) — the era in which they debuted is hardly comparable. And so, while Wael Mohya would rank third overall on the list, he would become the youngest Germany player in the modern era. The youngest to date was Hamburg legend Uwe Seeler in 1954, aged 17 years and 345 days.

#854. From Dunfermline to Dubai - McPake on new life in Middle East

James McPake may not have given up on football management but the former Dundee and Dunfermline Athletic boss is discovering there is life beyond the dugout.

Four months after moving to Dubai with his family, the 41-year-old has settled into a new role working in schools to develop young players.

It is a considerable change from the pressures of Scottish football but one that McPake and his family had been contemplating for more than a year.

His wife Dawn, a teacher, secured a position in Dubai before McPake landed his own opportunity, one that has opened up a different world of opportunities, including working alongside some recognisable names in football.

"It's certainly a bit different from back home but we're enjoying it," said McPake, who won an international cap with Northern Ireland in 2012.

"There is obviously a big demand for British curriculum teachers, so Dawn managed to get a position and I've been pretty fortunate to land here."

The timing of the family's move has inevitably attracted attention, given the wider tensions in the Middle East and concerns about security in the region.

However, McPake insists their experience of living in Dubai has been very different from some of the headlines.

"You don't hear a lot about it and you don't see anything. It is very much business as usual," he explains. "It's as busy as when we've come here on holiday. It's just like being anywhere else.

"The girls are enjoying it. They feel safe, they enjoy school and they can go out and play at night. We've had no issues that I've seen."

McPake's decision to head overseas has also provided an opportunity to step away from the demands of management and concentrate on developing players.

His responsibilities include overseeing under-16 and under-19 programmes at an impressive set-up, with school timetables adapted to accommodate training and facilities including strength and conditioning rooms, pools and pitches.

"The programme is relatively new but it's similar to the way you would look at an SFA performance school," he says. "The facilities are fantastic. It's difficult not to make a difference when you have facilities like these."

Former Real Madrid and Wales star Gareth Bale recently spent time at the school, answering questions from senior pupils during an hour-long session. And ex- England midfielder Jonjo Shelvey is also working full-time with McPake.

"For the kids, it was a fantastic experience," the former Livingston and Hibernian defender says.

"Gareth sat with myself and the head director of sport and answered question after question. Afterwards, we saw him out on the pitch with some of the younger kids, and Jonjo was on one of our other pitches.

"It's brilliant for the youngsters to have that sort of access to people who have played at the highest level."

McPake's departure from Scotland came at a time when opportunities were becoming increasingly difficult to secure. He admits that was a consideration in the move but not the driving force behind the family's decision.

There remains an obvious desire to return to the dugout but for now he is happy to embrace a different challenge.

"We've always wanted to give this a go, particularly for the girls. We wanted them to have an experience of a different society and culture and broaden their eyes to the world while they were still young," he says.

"The lack of opportunities in Scotland didn't make the decision for us but it certainly didn't cause us any hesitation when we were looking at coming out here.

"We've now been here for a few months, we're settled and we're used to life out here. It's been excellent and better than we imagined."

Although he is now thousands of miles away, McPake continues to follow Scottish football closely, particularly the fortunes of two clubs where he managed.

Dundee, where he was in charge between 2019 and 2022, have impressed him under Steven Pressley. And he also retains an affection for Dunfermline, where he won the League 1 title.

There is particular pride in watching youngsters he helped introduce to senior football begin to make their mark at a higher level.

"Luke Graham getting his first start for Scotland the other night was fantastic. He's a great kid and, even when he was really young and training with us at Dundee, you could see he was going to be the next one," says McPake, who played once for Northern Ireland.

McPake also keeps an eye on the progress of Dunfermline's Tod brothers, Andrew and Jon, who have both progressed through the Scotland international age groups.

There is also no lingering resentment towards either Dundee or Dunfermline, despite the manner in which his managerial spells ended.

McPake acknowledges that losing a job hurts but insists the affection he has for both clubs remains.

"At Dundee, it was excellent," he adds. "I have no bitterness towards them and Dunfermline is the same. We felt we weren't quite backed there.

"Should we have done better? Yes. But we won a very strong League 1 and then they just didn't push on in the Championship."
